title: First-Order Logic & Unification
html:
Propositional logic needs a separate symbol for every fact. First-order logic (FOL) adds objects, relations, functions and quantifiers, so one sentence can say something about all objects — “every king is a person”.

ElementExamplesDenotes
Constant symbolsJohn, Richard, 2Objects
Predicate symbolsKing(x), Brother(x, y), >Relations (true/false)
Function symbolsLeftLeg(x), Mother(x), +Functions returning objects
Variablesx, yRange over objects
Quantifiers∀x (for all), ∃x (there exists)Generality
EqualityFather(John) = HenryTwo terms name the same object

Translating English

EnglishFirst-order logic
All kings are persons∀x King(x) ⇒ Person(x)
King John has a crown on his head∃x Crown(x) ∧ OnHead(x, John)
Everybody loves somebody∀x ∃y Loves(x, y)
There is someone who is loved by everyone∃y ∀x Loves(x, y)
Nobody likes taxes¬∃x Likes(x, Taxes) ≡ ∀x ¬Likes(x, Taxes)
Brothers are siblings∀x, y Brother(x, y) ⇒ Sibling(x, y)
Do

Pair ∀ with ⇒ and ∃ with ∧: ∀x King(x) ⇒ Person(x); ∃x Crown(x) ∧ OnHead(x, John).

Avoid

∀x King(x) ∧ Person(x) (says everything is a king) or ∃x Crown(x) ⇒ OnHead(x, John) (true as soon as anything is not a crown).

Key point

Quantifier order matters: ∀x ∃y Loves(x, y) (everyone loves someone, maybe different people) is much weaker than ∃y ∀x Loves(x, y) (one person loved by all). Duality: ¬∀x P ≡ ∃x ¬P and ¬∃x P ≡ ∀x ¬P.

Unification

Unification — finding a substitution θ that makes two expressions identical: Unify(p, q) = θ where Subst(θ, p) = Subst(θ, q). The most general unifier (MGU) commits to as little as possible.

Inference in FOL

Generalised modus ponens lifts modus ponens with unification: from King(John), Greedy(y) and ∀x King(x) ∧ Greedy(x) ⇒ Evil(x), unify to θ = {x/John, y/John} and infer Evil(John) — only if Greedy(John) also unifies. Forward chaining with it gives Datalog-style reasoning. The classic crime KB:

MethodHowUsed in
Forward chainingGeneralised modus ponens from facts until nothing newDatalog, production systems, deductive databases
Backward chainingDepth-first from the goal, unifying with rule headsProlog, logic programming
ResolutionConvert to clausal form (Skolemise ∃), resolve with unificationAutomated theorem provers (Vampire, E)
Watch out

FOL entailment is only semi-decidable: if KB ⊨ α a complete procedure will eventually say so, but if not it may run forever. That's why practical systems restrict the language (Horn clauses, Datalog, description logics).

Why is first-order logic more expressive than propositional logic?

It has objects, relations, functions and quantifiers, so general rules (∀x King(x) ⇒ Person(x)) replace one propositional symbol per individual fact. It can describe infinite domains that propositional logic cannot.

What does unification do? Give an example.

It finds the most general substitution making two expressions identical. Knows(John, x) and Knows(y, Mother(y)) unify with {y/John, x/Mother(John)}. It's the core step of generalised modus ponens, Prolog and resolution.

What is the occurs check?

Before binding a variable x to a term, check that x does not occur inside that term — otherwise x = F(x) would create an infinite term. Prolog omits it by default for speed.
